**Wire verb `readers read-spectra`**: Read the scans of a spectra file: every scan's header always, and its peak arrays only on request.

# Wraps

- [`MsDataFileReader.GetDataFile`](https://github.com/smith-chem-wisc/mzLib/blob/23c2490e/mzLib/Readers/MsDataFileReader.cs) in `mzLib/Readers/MsDataFileReader.cs` at mzLib `23c2490e`
- [`MsDataFile.GetAllScansList`](https://github.com/smith-chem-wisc/mzLib/blob/23c2490e/mzLib/MassSpectrometry/MsDataFile.cs) in `mzLib/MassSpectrometry/MsDataFile.cs` at mzLib `23c2490e`
- [`SourceFile`](https://github.com/smith-chem-wisc/mzLib/blob/23c2490e/mzLib/MassSpectrometry/SourceFile.cs) in `mzLib/MassSpectrometry/SourceFile.cs` at mzLib `23c2490e`

# Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Unit | Range | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `path` (wire `--path`) | `path` | required | — | — | A spectra file: mzML, MGF, ms1/ms2 msalign, Thermo .raw, Bruker .d or timsTOF .d. |
| `ms_order` (wire `--ms-order`) | `int` | absent | — | `>= 1` | Keep only scans at this MS level. Applied BEFORE offset and limit, so ms-order 2 with limit 10 is the first ten MS2 scans. Given with no value is a usage error; absent means every level. |
| `offset` (wire `--offset`) | `int` | `0` | scans | `>= 0` | Skip this many scans (after the ms-order filter). |
| `limit` (wire `--limit`) | `int` | absent | scans | `>= 0` | Return at most this many scans. Absent means no limit. |
| `peaks` (wire `--peaks`) | `flag` | `false` | — | — | Include the mz and intensity arrays. Off by default because peaks are roughly the size of the file; combine with limit, a scan filter, or out. |
| `out` (wire `--out`) | `path` | absent | — | — | Write the table to this path as TSV instead of returning columns. Must differ from path. Peak arrays are written as ';'-joined lists. |

# Returns

Top-level fields:

| Field | Type | Unit | Null? | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | `string` | — | never | Absolute path of the input. |
| `file_type` | `string` | — | never | mzLib SupportedFileType name. |
| `reader` | `string` | — | never | The mzLib MsDataFile class that read it. |
| `scan_count` | `int` | scans | never | The file's true total, before any filter, so a filter matching nothing never looks like an empty file. |
| `ms_order` | `int` | — | yes: no ms-order filter was applied | The ms-order filter, echoed. |
| `record_count` | `int` | scans | never | Scans that passed the ms-order filter. |
| `returned_count` | `int` | scans | never | Scans in columns; 0 when written to out. |
| `offset` | `int` | scans | never | The offset applied. |
| `truncated` | `bool` | — | never | True whenever scans were left out by offset or limit. |
| `peaks_included` | `bool` | — | never | Whether mz and intensity columns are present. |
| `retention_time_unit` | `string` | — | never | Always "minutes" for this verb: every mzLib MsDataFile reader converts at the boundary. |
| `caveats` | `string[]` | — | never | Format-specific traps for THIS file; see caveats below. |
| `columns` (wire `column_names`) | `string[]` | — | never | Column order. |
| `columns` | `table` | — | yes: the table was written to out instead | Column name to per-scan values. |
| `output` | `object` | — | yes: out was not given | {path, format: "tsv", row\_count} when out was given. |
| `source` | `object` | — | yes: the reader built no source-file description at all (inner fields are null individually when the file does not record them) | {instrument\_model, instrument\_model\_accession, instrument\_serial\_number, acquisition\_start\_time, acquisition\_start\_time\_is\_utc} from mzLib SourceFile (\#1349). instrument\_model is the model NAME and instrument\_model\_accession its PSI-MS accession (mzML has both; Thermo .raw only the name, so the accession is null - match on the accession, never the name). acquisition\_start\_time is ISO-8601 text, ending in Z only when the source fixed the instant (mzML startTimeStamp with an offset); otherwise the acquisition PC's wall-clock time. acquisition\_start\_time\_is\_utc is never null: false means local instrument-PC time or absent, and is always false for Thermo .raw. Each inner field is null when the file does not record it (MGF and msalign record none). |
| `rows_not_read` | `int` | rows | yes: never counted for this verb | Always null. |
| `absent_fields` | `string[]` | — | never | Always empty for this verb: an unrecorded scan field is null per scan. |
| `failed_fields` | `string[]` | — | never | 'field: ExceptionType' for each column whose read threw on some scans; those cells are null. |
| `excluded_fields` | `object[]` | — | never | Always empty for this verb. |
| wire `error` | `object` | — | yes: always, for a single path: a file that cannot be read fails the call instead | {kind, type, message}; non-null only in a files\[\] entry under on-error skip. |

| `isolation_mz` | `float` | m/z | yes: MS1 scan, or not recorded | Isolation window centre. May be calibration-adjusted. |
| `isolation_width` | `float` | m/z | yes: MS1 scan, or not recorded | Isolation window width. |
| `selected_ion_mz` | `float` | m/z | yes: MS1 scan, or not recorded | Selected precursor m/z. May be calibration-adjusted. |
| `selected_ion_intensity` | `float` | intensity (instrument units) | yes: MS1 scan, or not recorded | Selected precursor intensity. |
| `selected_ion_charge_state_guess` | `int` | charge | yes: MS1 scan, or no charge assigned | Instrument or file charge-state guess. |
| `selected_ion_monoisotopic_guess_mz` | `float` | m/z | yes: MS1 scan, or no monoisotopic guess | Monoisotopic precursor m/z guess. |

| `hcd_energy` | `string` | — | yes: not HCD, or not recorded | Collision energy AS WRITTEN by the file (mzLib keeps it a string, e.g. "35" or "25,30,35"); not parsed. |
| `compensation_voltage` | `float` | V | yes: no FAIMS on this instrument | FAIMS compensation voltage. |
| `mz` | `float[]` | m/z | yes: scan has no spectrum | Peak m/z values. *Present only with `peaks`.* |
| `intensity` | `float[]` | intensity (instrument units) | yes: scan has no spectrum | Peak intensities, parallel to mz. *Present only with `peaks`.* |

# Errors

| Kind | mzLibRust returns | When |
|---|---|---|
| `usage` | [`MzLibError::Usage`](crate::MzLibError::Usage) | path missing or blank; file not found; the file is not one of the seven spectra types (the message names the views it does have) |
| `usage` | [`MzLibError::Usage`](crate::MzLibError::Usage) | ms-order, offset, limit or out given with no value; ms-order &lt; 1; offset or limit &lt; 0; non-integer value |
| `usage` | [`MzLibError::Usage`](crate::MzLibError::Usage) | out resolves to the same file as path |
| `correctness` | [`MzLibError::Bridge`](crate::MzLibError::Bridge) | a vendor format that cannot load on this platform surfaces as its real failure (Bruker/timsTOF native DLLs are Windows x64 only) |
| `usage` | [`MzLibError::Usage`](crate::MzLibError::Usage) | paths-stdin with path, offset or limit; paths-stdin with a value; no paths on stdin; a repeated path; threads 0 or below -1; on-error not fail or skip; on-error skip with a single path; out naming an input |
| `usage` | [`MzLibError::Usage`](crate::MzLibError::Usage) | with on-error fail, an input that is missing or not this view: the usage error of that input, prefixed 'Input &lt;i&gt; (&lt;path&gt;)' |
| `correctness` | [`MzLibError::Bridge`](crate::MzLibError::Bridge) | with on-error fail, mzLib failing to parse an input: that input's own error type, message prefixed 'Input &lt;i&gt; (&lt;path&gt;)' |
| `service_unavailable` | [`MzLibError::ServiceUnavailable`](crate::MzLibError::ServiceUnavailable) | never returned by this verb |

Any call can also fail on the way to mzLib or back, whatever the verb: [`MzLibError::BridgeNotFound`](crate::MzLibError::BridgeNotFound), [`MzLibError::Timeout`](crate::MzLibError::Timeout), [`MzLibError::Protocol`](crate::MzLibError::Protocol) or [`MzLibError::Io`](crate::MzLibError::Io).

# Caveats

- Headers only unless peaks is set; peak\_count tells you how many peaks, not what they are.
- Bruker .d and timsTOF .d need vendor native DLLs and read only on Windows x64. Thermo .raw is managed and reads everywhere.
- MGF: scan numbers may be file order; precursor scan is null unless the mzLib PRECURSORSCAN header is present; ms\_order comes from MSLEVEL or is inferred from PEPMASS; the scan window is derived from observed peaks.
- msalign holds DECONVOLVED neutral monoisotopic masses, not raw m/z: the mz column is not comparable with an mzML or raw file's mz and must not be re-deconvolved.
- msalign: scan\_window\_lower\_mz/\_upper\_mz are in m/z while the mz column is neutral MASS, so they are not on the same axis. mzLib synthesises the window by converting each mass back to m/z at its reported charge (MsAlign.cs:526); msalign records no window of its own.
- timsTOF .d is ion-mobility-resolved and this view flattens it: the mobility dimension is collapsed into scans and no 1/K0 value is reported.
- source.acquisition\_start\_time from a Thermo .raw is the acquisition PC's local clock (is\_utc false); ProteoWizard's mzML of the same run writes it as UTC assuming the CONVERTING machine's time zone, so the two can differ by the site's UTC offset (SourceFile.AcquisitionStartTime).
- Many files: --paths-stdin reads the list in ONE process, --threads at a time, into one long table with source\_index and source\_path first. The output does not depend on --threads (a tested property); the default of 1 is a memory choice, since every reader materialises the whole file.
